newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Analysts baffled by planned NBS deal.
newsitem.headline: Analysts baffled by planned NBS deal.

text.p: Analysts said on Tuesday that they were in the dark over a planned deal at South Africa's NBS Holdings Ltd, the country's fifth largest bank by market share, but more news was expected within days.
"It is a very well kept secret," said one analyst.
Earlier the firm issued a statement advising caution in trading in its shares as it was involved in talks that may have an effect on its share price.

A company spokesman declined to give further details, but said a further announcement was imminent. "We are not in a position to make any comment at this stage. We will have some comment in one or two days," she said.
The announcement has prompted feverish market speculation on the group's plans and its shares jumped 75 cents by 0803 GMT on Tuesday to stand at 65.50 rand.
"There will be a lot of interest in the stock this morning," one dealer said.
Analysts said they expected the move to be sizeable. "It should be a fairly significant transaction," one analyst said.

Some analysts said they expected the firm to stick to its core businesses of financial services, insurance and home loans. In May, NBS said it expected to grow by focusing closely on clients and developments in businesses that complemented its existing operations.
It said that it would report a real increase in earnings for the year to March 31, 1997, despite the turmoil in South Africa's financial markets and a slowdown in the economy.
The list of possible suitors or tie-up partners mentioned by analysts was long.
Analysts said the firm could be attempting to boost its insurance activities by negotiating closer links with RMB Holdings Ltd, which already owns 19.9 percent of the firm.
Insurance group Southern Life was also mentioned as potential partner, but some analysts said Southern would be too big for NBS.
The group's other main shareholders are Norwich Group with 21.3 percent and the Eskom Pension Fund with 10.7 percent.
One analyst said NBS was seen as being weak in asset management and investment banking. To this end a possible tie-up with Investec was mooted.
But analysts stressed the market was full of speculation. "It could be pretty much anything," one said.
They also said NBS put great store by its independence and, while this did not rule out a possible merger, it made it more unlikely.
One analyst, who said he had spoken to NBS executives, said a tie-up with black empowerment vehicle Real Africa Investments Ltd (Rail) was not on the cards.
Rail was mentioned in the announcement as a corporate advisor on the talks. "It doesn't have anything to do with Real Africa," the analyst said.
On October 3, international rating agency IBCA reaffirmed the domestic short-term A1 and long-term A ratings of NBS and said funding for any future expansion would not be a problem.
IBCA said that, given the resources of NBS' major shareholders, more capital could be made available for the group if needed.
-- Paul Harris, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
